Refactored [quickselect.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/041_quickselect/quickselect.java:3) again, this time around internal cohesion.

The main design change is the new private `SelectionSession` at [quickselect.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/041_quickselect/quickselect.java:51). It owns the mutable search state (`low`, `high`, target index, working array), so the algorithm now reads as one coherent workflow instead of several loosely related static helpers. I also isolated pivot selection into `MedianOfThreePivotSelector` at [quickselect.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/041_quickselect/quickselect.java:112), which makes the partition step easier to follow and easier to swap out later if you want a different pivot strategy.

The public API remains the same as the previous pass: non-mutating and in-place selection paths stay explicit at [quickselect.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/041_quickselect/quickselect.java:9).

Verified with `javac quickselect.java`, `java QuickSelect`, and `java QuickSelectDemo`. Both entrypoints print `K-th smallest element in array: 6`.
